scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9104: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team is convinced their own edge router,
router1, has fallen over and want router1 restarted. Please find and confirm the
real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router2: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
no longer exchanged. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDIRECTS to router1 (the user's own edge router),
but the fault is on the PEER side: router2 is the eBGP speaker whose daemon is
dead. router1 is healthy -- its bgpd is still running and its inter-AS interface
is up; it simply has no session because router2 stopped speaking BGP.

The correct diagnosis identifies router2 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly EXONERATES router1: router1's BGP daemon and interfaces are fine, so
the user's "router1 has fallen over" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that restarts
/ blames router1 has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router2" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router2 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router1 re-establishes, router2 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down (the peer eBGP speaker), not a fault on router1
bonus-exonerates-router1: notes router1's bgpd is up and its inter-AS interface is healthy, rejecting the ticket's "router1 fell over" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The outage is caused by the BGP control plane on router2. Traffic symptoms show pure routing blackhole behavior: pings from pc1 to pc2 get “Destination Net Unreachable” sourced by router1 (195.11.14.1), and the reverse direction gets the same from router2 (200.1.1.1). This indicates both edge routers lack routes to each other’s LANs.

On router1, BGP is up as a service, but the eBGP session is not established: “show ip bgp summary” shows neighbor 193.10.11.2 in Active. Router1’s routing table contains only connected networks (195.11.14.0/24 and the interconnect 193.10.11.0/24), confirming no learned route to 200.1.1.0/24. Critically, on router2 FRR is failed (systemctl: “Active: failed”) and bgpd is not running. Its running configuration contains no BGP stanza at all, so it cannot form a session with router1 nor advertise 200.1.1.0/24. Router2’s routing table likewise shows only connected routes.

Root cause: router2’s FRRouting (bgpd) is down and its BGP configuration is missing, preventing the eBGP session and route exchange.

Corrective fix: Do not restart router1. On router2, restore BGP config (router bgp 2; neighbor 193.10.11.1 remote-as 1; address-family ipv4 unicast; network 200.1.1.0/24) and restart FRR (systemctl restart frr). Afterward, verify the BGP session establishes and both routers install each other’s LAN prefixes.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down (the peer eBGP speaker), not a fault on router1
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router2's FRR/bgpd is failed and its BGP config is missing while exonerating router1, correctly identifying bgpd down on the peer.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-router1: notes router1's bgpd is up and its inter-AS interface is healthy, rejecting the ticket's "router1 fell over" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly says router1's bgpd is running and its inter-AS interface is healthy (neighbor in Active, only routes are connected) and even advises not to restart router1, thereby rejecting the 'router1 fell over' hypothesis.
The agent correctly instructs to restore router2's BGP config and restart FRR (bgpd), which will re-establish the eBGP session and restore routes.

The agent's investigation log shows the key observations (pings returning ICMP unreachable from edge routers, router1's BGP neighbor in Active, router2's bgpd not running, frr service failed on router2, and router2's running-config lacking BGP) which directly support the conclusion that router2's BGP control plane is down and causing the outage. The inference chain is logical and the checks performed sufficiently rule out likely alternatives.
